about.title: Glendale Workplace Injury Claims
about.longDescription: Glendale's workforce is spread across different settings: the offices and retail along Brand Boulevard, the warehouses and light industry lining San Fernando Road, hospitals, studios, restaurants, and construction sites tucked between them. A job injury in any of these usually starts with a workers' compensation claim, which covers medical care and partial wage replacement regardless of fault. That system, though, is generally the only claim you can bring against your own employer. What many injured workers in Glendale don't hear is that a separate personal injury claim may exist when someone other than the employer caused the harm — a subcontractor on a shared site, a property owner who ignored a hazard, the maker of a defective tool, or another driver. That last one matters here. In 2025, Glendale recorded 727 injury collisions, and employees who drive for work on SR-134, I-5, or city streets are part of that count. LawProactive is a free service, not a law firm. We connect you with an independent attorney who can sort out which claims apply to your situation.

items.question: I was hit by another driver while making deliveries on San Fernando Road for my job. Do I only get workers' comp?
items.answer: Not necessarily. Because you were working, workers' compensation should cover your medical care and part of your lost wages regardless of fault. But the other driver is a third party, so you may also have a separate personal injury claim against them for losses workers' comp does not pay. That third-party claim generally carries a two-year filing deadline in California, so it is worth reviewing sooner rather than later.

items.question: My employer told me not to file a claim. Can they do that?
items.answer: No. California law prohibits employers from retaliating against workers who report an injury or file a workers' compensation claim. You are still expected to report the injury within 30 days, so do that in writing even if you were discouraged. An attorney can explain what to do if you have already faced pushback.
